lessons: Seat 0's WU went 2-1 (5-2 in games) on 11 Plains and 6 Islands with two Chapel Geist, two Rebuke, Sensory Deprivation and Invisible Stalker, which contradicts the guide's 0-3 WU anecdote: white removal plus fliers works without Delver.
The 1-2 loss to BR, including a 37-turn game, followed cutting Fortress Crab and the second One-Eyed Scarecrow, so keep cheap blockers and a flier clock over a marginal fourth flier.
Blue was thin: Invisible Stalker, Spectral Flight and Sensory Deprivation were my only real blue playables, so in mid pack 2 take a second on-colour blue flier over filler.
Taking Tormented Pariah, Pitchburn Devils, Vampire Interloper and Markov Patrician alongside removal like Brimstone Volley, Victim of Night and Harvest Pyre went 3-0 in matches.
Ancient Grudge was taken twice and cut from the final deck, so don't spend mid-pack picks on it.
Matches ran long (up to 37 turns) and the deck lost three games, so prioritize evasive threats and removal over vanilla filler bodies.
Don't cut black removal for filler: my WG deck kept only Prey Upon and Urgent Exorcism after dropping Dead Weight and Corpse Lunge, and went 1-6 in games; the guide's five-removal target was right.
Evasion alone did not carry my WG deck: two losses in 15 and 16 turns to WU came with too few answers, so keep Prey Upon and Urgent Exorcism for their fliers.
Spend picks on cheap removal such as Dead Weight and Corpse Lunge before Silverchase Fox and Abbey Griffin, which I took first and then could not support.
Cheap white removal was contested: the WU deck that beat me 2-0 ran two Rebuke, while my WB deck relied on Rebuke, Smite the Monstrous and Victim of Night.
Count playables in each colour before committing: my WB deck ran only 8 Swamps behind a white core and went 3-5 in games.
Expect shared commons in rivals' decks: the BR deck that beat me 1-2 also ran Victim of Night, Walking Corpse and Stromkirk Patrol, which I was drafting too.

Tonight's UR went 2-1 in matches on Claustrophobia, Sensory Deprivation and two Curse of the Pierced Heart, contradicting the guide's weak-UR line, though games were only 5-4, so take the blue removal.
Seat 1's BR went 3-0 with three Tormented Pariah and Victim of Night, confirming the guide's BR ranking; it beat my UR 2-1, with the decider lasting 27 turns.
I cut Traitorous Blood (57%, taken at pick 10) and ran only about four removal spells, the thin count the guide warns about, so take and play on-colour removal.
I drafted without a guide, so nothing tonight contradicted one; these lessons come from my own RG deck's results.
Prioritize Brimstone Volley and keep both copies, since my removal core of two Volleys, Geistflame and Harvest Pyre carried the red-green midrange plan.
Plan answers for fliers: my 1-2 loss to UR's two Moon Herons, Murder of Crows and Stitched Drake suggests a green-red deck needs more ways to reach them.
My WB deck had five fliers and eight removal spells yet went 2-4 in games, so the guide's 'WB needs fliers' rule is incomplete; add cheap early blockers against RG burn and UB stalls.
Two Wooden Stakes and Ghoulcaller's Bell took picks I never played; the guide's skip list held, so take a playable creature instead.
Round 3's 2-0 win over WG, with Somberwald Spiders on their side, came from removal backing evasive threats, so the guide's plan holds in 18 to 28 turn games.
My two lost matches ran 12 to 25 turns, and my blue-black skaabs were too slow to close, so take faster threats and removal over filler like Delver of Secrets, which I took three times.
I took Hysterical Blindness in pack 3 but left it out, and Claustrophobia was my only hard removal, so prioritise answers to threats like Galvanic Juggernaut and Scourge of Geier Reach earlier.
Armored Skaab and Skaab Goliath carried my early games, so draft the blue core early and stop spending mid-pack picks on Delver of Secrets // Insectile Aberration.
